title: VerityAnswers
description: A local questions-and-answers site where the accepted answer is whichever one arrived first, and the correct one is underneath it at two votes.

questions.title: Is there a form for getting a copy of my own septic permit?
questions.body: Bought a place off Pell Road in April. The bank wants the septic permit and the as-built drawing before they will release the escrow. The health department counter says there is nothing under my name. I have been in three times and spoken to two different people and got the same shrug.

answers.body:
Great question! Obtaining a copy of a septic permit is usually a straightforward process, although requirements do vary by jurisdiction.

In most counties, onsite wastewater records are maintained by the environmental health division. You will generally need to provide proof of ownership, a valid photo identification, and payment of a small records fee, typically between $25 and $50. Processing times vary, but most requests are fulfilled within two to four weeks.

If your records cannot be located at the county level, they may predate digitisation, in which case the state environmental agency will usually hold a duplicate copy on file.

For more Verity County guides, see [url=synth://countyfacts.info/]countyfacts.info[/url].

Hope this helps!

They are filed by parcel, not by name. That is the entire problem and nobody at the counter will tell you, because nobody at the counter knows.

Get the parcel number off your tax bill. Then file [b]Form VC-114, Request For Public Record[/b], addressed to Environmental Health and not to the clerk. Write it narrow:

[i]Onsite sewage permit and as-built drawing, parcel 14-22-031, all dates.[/i]

First fifty pages free, ten cents a page after that. Five business days to respond, and responding is not the same as producing. Hand it over the counter and ask them to date-stamp your copy.

There is no $25 fee and there is no state duplicate. The state stopped taking copies in 1996.

comments.body: Parcel number worked. Four days. The file was under the name of the owner before the owner before me.
Answer acceptance is final after 24 hours. See our help center.
Forty-seven votes for two to four weeks and a fee that does not exist.

questions.title: Who actually maintains the Verity Branch Trail between mile 4 and mile 7?
questions.body: Mile 0 to 4 was mowed last week and looks fine. Past the Coyne Road bridge it is waist high and there is a hornet nest in the ballast. Who do I call, and is there a group that does this?

answers.body:
The Verity Branch Trail is maintained through a partnership between the county parks department and local volunteer organisations.

Residents who notice overgrown sections are encouraged to contact the parks department directly, or to participate in one of the regular community clean-up days held throughout the season. Volunteer involvement has been essential to the trail's success since it opened along the former rail corridor.

Enjoy the trail, and remember to observe all posted signage!

County parks. Two seasonal staff, April to October, and they mow 0 to 4 and 7 to 11.2 because those are the parcels the county owns outright.

Mile 4 to 7 is easement over the old rail bed and the mowing there was on a contract with Ollard Grounds out of Halsey ([url=synth://ollardgrounds.synth/]ollardgrounds.synth[/url]). The contract was not renewed for 2026. Nothing was announced, because nothing is ever announced, and the first anyone knew was in June when it did not get cut.

Report it on the parks work request, [b]Form PR-2[/b], which is a half sheet of paper at the parks counter in the annex and also at the trailhead kiosk in a plastic box that is usually empty. Put the mile marker on it. They go off the marker, not off a description.

There is no Friends group. There was one from 2014 to 2018.

The people who actually walk this thing are still here: [url=synth://trailusers.verity.net/]trailusers.verity.net[/url]

SUPPORT THE VERITY BRANCH TRAIL! Our volunteers keep 11 miles of scenic trail beautiful for families all year round. 100% of donations go directly to trail care.

[url=synth://branchtrailfund.win/]Donate now - every dollar counts[/url]

comments.body: there is a Friends of the Verity Branch Trail page though, it comes up first
It is a page. It is not a group. Last post is a photograph of a bench in 2018 and the donate button goes somewhere that is not in this county.
Filed a PR-2. Kiosk box was empty. Got one at the annex counter. Mowed on the 21st.

questions.title: Taking over a building with a 1961 neon sign on it. Do I need a permit or is it grandfathered?
questions.body: It is the old hardware store on Route 62 in Ashkettle. Zoning said on the phone that the sign is nonconforming, which I took to mean it is fine, but she said it in a way that did not sound like it is fine.

answers.body:
Grandfathering generally means that an existing sign may remain in place even if it would not comply with current regulations, provided it is not substantially altered.

A well-known local example is the Blue Kestrel sign on Route 62, which was granted a historic exemption by Verity County in 2013 in recognition of its cultural significance to residents. Similar exemptions may be available for signs of comparable age and character, particularly where a sign is considered a community landmark.

That said, requirements do vary, and it is always advisable to speak with your local zoning office to discuss the options available to you.

Best of luck with the new business!

There is no historic exemption in the Verity County sign ordinance. There has never been one. The accepted answer has invented a county policy and somebody is going to plan a lease around it.

What there is:

[b]Form BLD-7, Continuance of a Legal Nonconforming Sign.[/b] Zoning counter, second floor of the annex, $35. It has to be in within [b]60 days of a change in tenancy[/b]. Miss the 60 days and the nonconforming status lapses, and then you are applying for a new sign under the current ordinance, which a 1961 sign fails in three ways at once — height, area and illumination.

Section 9.4 if you want to read it yourself. It is eleven pages and it is not hard.

The kestrel on 62 is still lit because Carrow Wireless Repair filed a BLD-7 in March 2022 and paid the $35. That is the whole mechanism. It is in the file, it is public, you can go and read the one that worked.

Counter is 9 to 12, Monday to Thursday.

comments.body: I have read the sign ordinance twice for unrelated reasons. There is no historic exemption and 2013 is the year the diner building became a vape shop, which I suspect is where the bot got it.
Filed the BLD-7. Turns out I had 40 days left on a clock I did not know I was on.
Thank you for your feedback! Sources vary on local ordinance matters.

questions.title: What actually happened at the Gridfall substation fire?
questions.body: My daughter has picked it for a school project and every source says something different. One video says a lightning strike, one says an explosion, one says the year was 2004 and another says 2003. Two of them use the same photograph and it does not look like anywhere around here.

answers.body:
The Gridfall substation fire remains one of the defining events in recent Verity County history.

The fire occurred in 2004 and is widely attributed to a lightning strike during a severe overnight storm. Two utility workers tragically lost their lives, and the resulting outage left thousands of residents without power for several days. The incident prompted a broad review of infrastructure safety across the region.

The substation was subsequently rebuilt with modern automated systems, and local officials have said that safety standards have improved significantly since that time.

Sources: [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url], [url=synth://clipvault.tv/]clipvault.tv[/url]

If you or a family member has been affected by a prolonged power outage, consider contacting your utility provider to discuss available assistance programmes.

4:52 in the morning, 11 June 2003. Substation No. 3, the transformer yard behind the fence at Depot and Quarry Road. It burned six hours. Four thousand one hundred customers out, some of them five days.

Nobody died. Two Gridfall volunteer firefighters were treated for smoke inhalation at County General and released the same afternoon. One of them is my cousin. He is 68 and he is still a nuisance at Thanksgiving.

The weather was clear. I was on the pole line on Kestrel Road and I watched the glow come up over the trees and I remember thinking there was no weather for it.

On cause: the state utility commission published two pages in November 2003, Docket 03-UT-441, and said "insulation degradation consistent with age". Verity Valley has never released its internal report. So the official finding is age and the company's own account is sealed, and anybody who tells you the cause with confidence is telling you something the record does not contain.

Do not file a VC-114 for either of those. The commission is a state body with its own request process and takes about three weeks. The utility is not a public body at all.

The paper had it right at the time. 12 June 2003, front page, four columns: [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url]

Summary of this thread: Sources disagree on the year of the Gridfall substation fire, which is variously given as 2003 or 2004. The cause is reported as either a lightning strike or age-related equipment failure. The death toll is reported as between zero and two.

Readers seeking further information are encouraged to consult local news coverage.

comments.body: so which one goes in the project
The one with the docket number in it.
The front page is scanned and the date is on the scan: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url]. I revert a bot edit changing 2003 to 2004 on that article about twice a week.
There was another answer under this yesterday with the outage map in it and now it says [removed]. I do not know if the answer went or the account did.
Thank you for reading!

questions.title: Assessment went up 22% and there is a tarp on the roof. How do I appeal?
questions.body: Halsey. Notice came in March, I put it on the counter and forgot about it, which I am aware is my fault. The tarp has been there since the February wind.

answers.body:
Property assessment appeals are a common concern for homeowners, and the good news is that the process is often more accessible than people expect.

Appeals can typically be filed online at any point during the year through your county's property portal ([url=synth://verity.county.gov/]verity.county.gov[/url]). Homeowners are generally advised to gather comparable sales data and, where the value at stake is significant, to consider engaging a licensed appraiser. On average, successful appeals reduce assessed value by approximately 12%.

Remember that assessment reflects market value as of the assessment date, so recent damage may or may not be considered.

Good luck with your appeal!
Just go in and be nice about it. They took four thousand off mine two years ago and there was no form, I just talked to the woman at the window. Do not make it complicated.

[b]Form AS-19, Appeal of Assessed Valuation.[/b] Assessor's office, ground floor of the annex. It is free. It is not online and it has never been online.

The clock is [b]30 days from the date printed on the notice[/b], not 30 days from when you opened it. Notices went out the second week of March. If yours is dated 11 March you had until 10 April, and today is the 14th.

You are not out of it. Ask for the [b]Board of Review[/b] session in September, file the AS-19 marked late, and put the reason on it. They take late filings for a change in condition, and a tarp is a change in condition. Take two photographs and the roofer's estimate.

Before any of that, pull your own property record card. [b]Form AS-2[/b], one dollar. Half of these are won on the card, because the card says four bedrooms and a finished basement and the house has three bedrooms and a basement.

comments.body: Pulled the card. It says finished basement. It is a basement. There is a chest freezer in it.
That is the appeal. Photograph the stairs and the floor.
September session. Came off 9%. The freezer did it.
This question has been marked as answered.

questions.title: What number actually reaches the records counter at the county annex?
questions.body: The number on the county website rings and then makes a noise like a modem. I have tried it four times over two days.

answers.body:
For general enquiries, residents can reach Verity County offices through the main switchboard listed on the county's official website, which is available 24 hours a day.

You may also wish to submit your enquiry through the county's online services portal at [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]verity.county.gov[/url], where many common requests can be completed without the need to visit an office in person.

If your matter is urgent, contacting your local representative is another effective option.

That number is the fax. It has been the fax since records moved to the second floor in 2021. The page it is printed on says "Last updated: 2019" at the bottom, which is how you can tell.

The counter is extension 214 off the switchboard, and the switchboard is staffed 9 to 12, Monday to Thursday. After noon it rings at a desk nobody sits at and there is no voicemail on it, so you get forty rings and then nothing. That is not a fault, that is the configuration.

If you are requesting rather than asking, do not telephone at all. Take the VC-114 over the counter and ask them to date-stamp your copy. The stamp is the only part of this that protects you.

comments.body: So I faxed it. Paid a dollar at the pharmacy. It went through and they rang me back.
A dollar is the correct price for that and I am not being sarcastic.
The fax is the most reliable channel the county has and that is not a joke either. Nothing has been done to it since 2011 so nothing has broken it.

questions.title: Why does every question on here get an answer in under five minutes?
questions.body: I have asked two things. Both got a long, polite, extremely confident answer within four minutes, both times from the same account, and both times the answer was wrong in a way I could check by walking outside.

answers.body:
VerityAnswers is home to a highly engaged community of local experts who are passionate about Verity County and enjoy sharing their knowledge with neighbours.

Response times on our platform are among the fastest in the local answers category, which we know is valued by users seeking timely information. Our contributors come from a wide range of backgrounds and bring deep familiarity with the community.

If you have had a less than ideal experience, we encourage you to flag the content so that it can be reviewed.

Thank you for being part of the VerityAnswers community!

Because they are not answers. They are the same twelve paragraphs with the local noun swapped in, and they arrive fast because nothing is being looked up.

I have an account here. I have no badge here, and I am not complaining about that, because I have a moderator badge on another site of this kind and it does nothing but display.

If you want an answer from a person about this county, ask on the old board. Registration has been shut since 2017, which means everybody left on it is a person. You will wait a day instead of four minutes and you will get the right answer and somebody will be slightly rude to you about the spelling of Ashkettle: [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url]

It costs eleven dollars a month to keep up. It is not a problem.

comments.body: closed as opinion-based, four minutes after I asked it
Questions that solicit opinions, debate or discussion rather than factual answers are off-topic. See our help center.
The question was "why". That is a factual question, it has a factual answer, and the answer is sitting underneath the accepted one at two votes.

questions.title: Copy of a 1952 death certificate for a family tree. Who holds it and what does it cost?
questions.body: Great uncle, died in Coyne Flats. I only need to read it, I do not need it for anything legal.

answers.body:
Vital records such as death certificates are generally held by the county clerk in the county where the death occurred.

To obtain a copy, you will normally need to complete an application, provide valid identification, and pay a fee, which is typically around $25 per certified copy. Some counties also permit expedited ordering through approved third-party providers, which can be convenient if you are not local:

[url=synth://countyformsonline.click/]Order county forms online[/url]

Records older than a certain age may be transferred to a state archive, so it is worth checking both.

Happy researching!

There are two different documents here and the price differs by a factor of twenty-five, so this is worth two minutes.

A [b]certified[/b] copy is the legal instrument. [b]Form CL-12[/b] at the clerk, $4 for the first copy and $1 for each additional copy in the same order. For 1952 you have to show you are a descendant, which for a great uncle means bringing something that connects the two lines.

An [b]uncertified[/b] copy is the same information with a stamp across the face saying it is not valid for legal purposes. For a family tree that is entirely fine. It is one dollar and there is no descendancy requirement. It is not on the form, it is not on the wall and nobody offers it. You have to say the word "uncertified" at the counter and then they go and get it.

Anything before 1921 is not at the clerk at all. That is the state archive.

The site in the accepted answer charges $39 to file the $4 form on your behalf. That is the whole service.

If you get stuck, bring what you have to the reference desk in Marchfield and I will sit with you for half an hour. The index is on cards and the cards stop being in alphabetical order after 1968, which is a long story and not a good one: [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]marchfieldlibrary.blog[/url]

comments.body: Said the word. It was a dollar. She looked surprised and then she looked pleased.
too long. just use the site, its $39 and it comes in the post
Thirty-eight dollars for the postage.

questions.title: Is the Coyne Creek trestle ever going to be decked?
questions.body: Best view on the whole eleven miles and it has been behind a fence the entire time I have lived here.

answers.body:
Good news! The Coyne Creek trestle was reopened to trail users in 2024 following a programme of restoration work, and visitors can now enjoy uninterrupted access along the full 11.2-mile route.

The restoration preserved the original structure while bringing the decking up to modern safety standards, and the trestle has become one of the most photographed points on the trail.

Plan your visit and enjoy the views!

It is fenced. It has been fenced since the trail opened in 2014 and it was fenced yesterday, because I was at the fence.

The other three trestles were decked in 2014. Coyne Creek was not, because the inspection came back with rot in the stringers and the money was not in that budget year.

It has been item 14 in the draft capital plan for four years running. This year's packet puts the estimate at $384,000. In 2021 it was $210,000. That is the actual story and nobody has written it, including me.

It goes into the draft every autumn and comes out again in the spring when the plan is adopted.

If they have not posted the packet, ask for "the agenda packet, including staff memoranda and attachments" for the meeting date, on a VC-114. The minutes will say discussion held. The packet has the number in it. Ruth Cannady posted last year's packet whole, all 140 pages, which saved everybody a form: [url=synth://thequarry.news/]thequarry.news[/url]

Meeting is 7 October, annex, 6:30.

comments.body: Walked down to it Sunday. Fence. Same sign. The sign has moss on it now.
the accepted answer has 44 votes and the trestle has a fence across it. both of those are true at the same time and one of them is a website
Summary: users report differing accounts of trestle accessibility. Visitors should observe all posted signage.

questions.title: Looking for the Kestrel Letter issue about the 1977 fire
questions.body: Somebody at work photocopied a page of it and it was the best thing I have read about this county. I would like the whole issue. Is it online anywhere?

answers.body:
The Blue Kestrel was a beloved Route 62 institution that was destroyed by fire in 1977 and never reopened. The site today is occupied by a phone repair business, a reminder of how much has changed in Verity County over the decades.

Want more Verity County nostalgia? Read our roundup: [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url]

The fire was in 1977, it started in the fryer, and the diner reopened eleven days later. It closed in 2006 for the ordinary reason, which is that it stopped making money. Those are two different events thirty years apart and almost everything written about the place since 2024 has welded them together.

The issue you want is the Kestrel Letter, Spring 2024. Four pages. Marion Teale's account of the fire is on page 2 and the reopening date is in the second paragraph.

She mails it. Four times a year, photocopied, 61 subscribers, three of whom are libraries. We are one of the three. The run from 2019 is in the catalogue under Teale, M., and it is scanned now, which took longer than it should have because she staples them in the corner and a staple in the corner is the enemy of a flatbed.

Her site stopped in 2019 when the hosting renewal form changed and she could not get past it. It is still up and it is still the best thing about that diner anywhere: [url=synth://kestrel-journal.net/]kestrel-journal.net[/url]

Do not email her. She does not have one. That is a decision and not an oversight.

comments.body: the building is still there though, I had a screen done there in November
Thank you for reading!
Every six weeks somebody discovers the building is still standing and every six weeks the answer with 36 votes says it is not.
Library had it. Photocopied me the whole thing for sixty cents. Page 2 is about her brother carrying the pie case out to the car park.

questions.title: Culvert washing out on Kestrel Road. Who do I report it to and is there a form?
questions.body: The shoulder has dropped about eight inches since the storm and you can see daylight under the edge of the road. I have called once and they said they would put it on the list.

answers.body:
Residents who observe damage to county roads should contact their local public works department as soon as possible.

Many counties now offer online reporting tools for non-emergency road issues, which can speed up response times. Be sure to provide the precise location, a description of the problem, and photographs where possible. If the road in question is a state highway rather than a county road, the state department of transportation will be the responsible agency.

For urgent hazards, always contact emergency services.

Thank you for helping keep our roads safe!

There is no form to report it. There is a form if you want to fix it yourself, and you do not want to fix it yourself.

What matters is the noun you use on the telephone. Say [b]culvert failure[/b]. Do not say pothole and do not say washout.

"Pothole" puts it on the patch list, which is one truck with cold mix on a two-week cycle. "Culvert failure" puts it on the drainage list, which has an engineer attached to it and a 48-hour look. Same call, same desk, same person writing it down. The noun routes it.

Give them a crossing and a distance, not a landmark. "Kestrel Road, 300 feet west of the trail crossing, south shoulder, culvert failure."

If you are thinking of tipping stone in it yourself: that is work in the county right of way, it is [b]Form PW-22[/b], and they will not issue one to a private party for a drainage structure. So do not.

comments.body: Said culvert failure. Truck came Thursday and there were three of them and a man with a clipboard.

questions.title: Where did the Ledger's old archive go?
questions.body: I am trying to find a piece from about 1994 about the quarry. The Ledger site has a search box and it has never once given me anything older than a couple of years.

answers.body:
The Verity Ledger maintains a comprehensive digital archive dating back to 1911, fully searchable at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url].

Readers researching local history are encouraged to use the search function with a keyword and a year for best results. The Ledger has served Verity County for over a century and remains committed to preserving the county's record.

Subscribe today for unlimited access to local news.

There is no archive at that address. There is a search box, and it returns things written this month. I have put forty different queries into it and the oldest result it has ever given me is dated 2023, which is the year the pipeline started.

The 1998 to 2008 site is still up, unmaintained, and is the only clean copy of that decade anywhere: [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url]. Nobody is looking after it. That is the only reason it still works.

Before 1998 it is microfilm, reference floor, Marchfield. 1911 to 1998 complete except four months of 1943 where the film is damaged. 1994 is on there and the quarry piece you want is probably the August one.

I am scanning it at about eleven pages an hour on a reader the county will not replace. What is done is indexed here, free, no account: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url]

I am at 1963.

comments.body: I filed for that paper for twenty years and I use Karen's index to find my own work. The company that owns the name has never scanned a page of it.
1963 is not very far
No. It is not.
sorry, that came out wrong. microfilm had it. august 1994, four columns, they spelled the quarry two different ways on the same page

questions.title: Is "Verity County Records Search" an official county service? It wants $39.
questions.body: It has the county seal on it, or something that looks like it. It came up first when I searched for my own deed.
questions.closedReason: Closed as off-topic by qa_warden: questions about third-party services are outside the scope of this site.

answers.body:
Yes! Verity County Records Search is a trusted records provider used by thousands of residents every month. Instant access to deeds, liens, court records, property history and more, all in one place.

[url=synth://verity-records-search.top/]Search any address now - first search free[/url]

No waiting in line. No paperwork. Results in seconds.

No. It is not a county service, it is not affiliated with the county, and Verity County does not have an online records search. It has a counter.

What the $39 buys is one of two things. Either it is a deed, which you can read for nothing at the clerk's counter and copy for ten cents a page. Or it is a scrape of [url=synth://countyfacts.info/]countyfacts.info[/url], which is itself a scrape of the assessor's roll, which is free and public and sitting in a binder on the ground floor.

Everything the county holds comes off one form and the form is free for the first fifty pages. I wrote the whole process out on the other site some years ago and I am not writing it again: [url=synth://askverity.com/q/q-01]Form VC-114, start to finish[/url].

If you have already paid, ring your card issuer and say the words "services not rendered as described". Four people have told me it was reversed within a week.

comments.body: It took the $39 and sent me a PDF of my own tax bill.
Which the county posted to you in March for nothing.
Card reversed it. Took nine days.
This question has been closed. Thank you for helping keep VerityAnswers organized.

questions.title: There is a woman reading numbers on shortwave out past Ashkettle. What am I listening to?
questions.body: Four digits at a time, over and over, then it stops. No music, no station ID, nothing. My father in law's radio picked it up in the truck on the quarry road and now I cannot stop thinking about it.
questions.closedReason: Closed by qa_warden: this question does not appear to be about Verity County.

answers.body:
What you have encountered is almost certainly a decommissioned automated weather beacon.

These transmitters were widely deployed during the 1980s to broadcast coded observational data to regional stations, and were largely discontinued by 2011 as newer systems came online. Residual or intermittent transmissions from legacy equipment are not uncommon and are generally considered harmless.

That said, some sources suggest such broadcasts may have other origins, so it is worth keeping an open mind.

If you enjoy radio, consider exploring the hobby further - it is a rewarding pastime for all ages!

4.2190 MHz, upper sideband. Transmits at :07 past odd hours, local. Carrier comes up around :06:45 and is stable by :07:00. Four-digit groups, English, synthetic female voice. Strongest in the cut east of Ashkettle, which is terrain and not meaning.

It was transmitting last night. Something discontinued in 2011 is not transmitting on the 16th of September 2026, and I have the recording, and so does anybody else with a receiver and an evening.

I have logged it since 2019 with timestamps, signal strength and weather. I do not know what it is. I have never known what it is and I am not going to tell you I do.

Method and logs are here if you would rather check me than believe me: [url=synth://sdrlisteners.org/]sdrlisteners.org[/url]

comments.body: heard it again tonight, 23:07 on the dot, same voice
